skills.title: Name family members and the ways they care for and help each other
Recognise that families differ in size and in who is part of them
Explain why sharing household work matters and that anyone in a family can do it

expectations: Families can be big or small: some have grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins; some have one parent; some children live with grandparents.
Family members care for each other by sharing work (cooking, cleaning, fetching things, earning) and by looking after anyone who is sick or sad.
Any family member — men and women, boys and girls, elders and children — can do household work.
Children help too, with jobs that suit their age.
There is no single 'right' kind of family; different families are all real families.

misconceptions.belief: Every family looks like my own — same size and same members (always a mother, a father and children).
signs: Says a family without a mother or a father 'is not a real family'
Is surprised that grandparents, uncles and cousins can all live together
Says every family has four people

diagnostic.prompt_en: Zoya lives with her nani and her mother. Tenzin lives with eleven people — grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins. Which of these is a family?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Zoya apni nani aur mummy ke saath rehti hai. Tenzin ke ghar mein gyaarah log hain — dada-dadi, chacha-chachi aur cousins. Batao, inme se family kaunsi hai?

options.text: Both are families
Only Tenzin's, because a family must be big
Neither — a family must have a mummy, a papa and children

remediation.representation: Picture gallery of four different Indian families: joint family, small family, single parent, grandparents raising a grandchild
remediation.moveShape: Contrasting cases: ask first what is the SAME in all four (they live together and care for each other), only then what is different

misconceptions.belief: Household work like cooking and cleaning is only for mothers and girls.
signs: Says 'cooking is mummy's work'
Assigns every chore card to women or girls
Laughs at the idea of a father or brother sweeping

diagnostic.prompt_en: Who can cook, sweep or wash clothes at home?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ghar mein khaana banana, jhaadu lagana ya kapde dhona — yeh kaun kar sakta hai?

options.text: Only mothers and girls
Anyone in the family — men, women, boys and girls
Only grown-ups, never children

remediation.representation: Chore-sort game where any family member card can be dragged onto any chore
remediation.moveShape: Ask for a real counter-example the child already knows (a father, uncle, brother or a famous chef who cooks), then ask what that example tells us

misconceptions.belief: Children are too small to help; only grown-ups take care of the family.
signs: Says 'I'm small, I don't do anything at home'
Cannot name a single way a child helps

diagnostic.prompt_en: Arjun is 8 years old. Can he help his family at home?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Arjun 8 saal ka hai. Kya woh ghar mein family ki madad kar sakta hai?

options.text: Yes — he can do small jobs like filling water bottles or watering plants
No — children are too small to help

remediation.representation: A ladder of age-suitable jobs (keep own shoes, fill bottles, water plants, lay plates)
remediation.moveShape: Let the child pick one job they already do or could do, and name who it helps

items.prompt_en: Name two things people in a family do to take care of each other.
items.prompt_hi: Achha batao, ek family mein log ek doosre ka khayal kaise rakhte hain? Koi do kaam batao.
items.answer: Any two caring acts, e.g. cooking food, looking after someone who is sick, fetching milk, helping with homework, telling bedtime stories.
acceptable: taking care when someone is sick
hints: Think about your morning before school — who does what?
Think about food, clothes, and what happens when someone is unwell.
Someone makes the ___ and someone helps when you are ___.
Cooking food and caring for someone who is sick are two ways families care.

items.prompt_en: Meera lives with her papa and her dadi. Is that a family? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Meera apne papa aur dadi ke saath rehti hai. Kya yeh family hai? Kyun?
items.answer: Yes. They live together and care for each other; families come in many shapes and sizes.
acceptable: yes, they care for each other
haan, family hai kyunki woh ek doosre ka khayal rakhte hain
hints: What makes a group of people a family?
Do Meera, her papa and dadi look after each other?
A family is people who ___ for each other.
Yes — it is a family, because they live together and care for each other.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: in a house with twelve people, what would happen by evening if only ONE person did all the cooking, cleaning and washing?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: ek ghar mein baarah log hain. Agar saara khaana, safaai aur kapde sirf EK insaan kare, toh shaam tak kya hoga?
items.answer: That person would be very tired and the work might not get finished; when the work is shared, it gets done and nobody is over-tired.
hints: Imagine doing twelve people's work alone.
How would your body feel after that much work?
One person doing everything gets very ___.
They would be exhausted and the work would pile up — sharing makes it manageable.

items.prompt_en: Dadi is sick in bed today. Before I tell you — what do you think the others in the family will do differently?
items.prompt_hi: Aaj dadi ki tabiyat kharab hai, woh bed pe hain. Socho — ghar ke baaki log aaj kya alag karenge?
items.answer: They will take over her jobs and look after her: bring water and medicine, cook, keep her company, keep the house quiet.
hints: Who usually does dadi's jobs when she's well?
Think of two things: her work, and dadi herself.
Others will do her ___ and take care of ___.
The family shares her jobs and looks after her until she's better.

items.prompt_en: Why is it good when everyone in a family shares the housework?
items.prompt_hi: Ghar ka kaam sab milke karein, toh yeh achha kyun hai?
items.answer: The work gets done faster, no one gets too tired, and everyone learns to care for each other.
hints: What happens when one person does it all?
Think about time and tiredness.
Shared work gets done ___ and nobody gets too ___.
Sharing means work finishes faster and no single person is worn out.

items.prompt_en: Aman lives with his mummy, papa and baby sister. Lalita lives with her grandparents, two uncles, two aunts and four cousins. What is different about these families, and what is the same?
items.prompt_hi: Aman mummy, papa aur choti behen ke saath rehta hai. Lalita dada-dadi, do chacha, do chachi aur chaar cousins ke saath rehti hai. In dono families mein kya alag hai aur kya same hai?
items.answer: Different: their size and who lives there (a small family and a joint family). Same: they live together and care for each other.
acceptable: one is small, one is a joint family; both care for each other
ek choti family, ek joint family; dono khayal rakhte hain
hints: Count the people in each home.
Now think: what do both families do for their members?
Different in ___; same because they both ___.
Different size and members; the same because both care for each other.

items.prompt_en: Name one job a child of your age can do at home to help the family.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari umar ka bachcha ghar mein family ki madad ke liye kaunsa ek kaam kar sakta hai?
items.answer: Any age-suitable job, e.g. filling water bottles, watering plants, laying plates, folding clothes, keeping own shoes and books in place.
hints: Think of something small you've seen yourself do.
Something with water bottles, plants or plates?
I can ___ the plants or fill the water ___.
For example, watering the plants or filling the water bottles — children help too.

items.prompt_en: Your class is going on a picnic. Name two jobs that need doing and say how the class could share them.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari class picnic pe ja rahi hai. Do kaam batao jo karne padenge, aur class unhe kaise baant sakti hai?
items.answer: Any two jobs (carrying mats, packing food, filling water, cleaning up after) shared among children and teachers so it gets done quickly.
acceptable: carry mats and clean up, everyone takes a part
pack food and fill water bottles in groups
hints: What needs to happen before, during and after a picnic?
Who could do each job — one person or many?
Jobs like ___ and ___ can be split between groups.
For example: one group carries mats, another cleans up — sharing makes it quick.

items.prompt_en: Sparrows have families too. Both the mother and the father sparrow bring food to their babies in the nest. What does this tell you about who does caring work?
items.prompt_hi: Gauraiya ki bhi family hoti hai. Ghosle mein bachchon ko mummy gauraiya aur papa gauraiya — dono khaana laate hain. Isse caring ke kaam ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
items.answer: Caring work can be shared by both parents — it is not only one person's job.
acceptable: dono mil ke dekhbhaal karte hain
hints: Who feeds the baby sparrows?
Is it only the mother?
Both ___ share the caring.
It shows caring can be shared by both parents, in birds and in people.

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a family tree: Dada and Dadi at the top; below them Papa and Chacha; below Papa is Anu. Who is Anu's grandmother? Say it, then tap her box.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe ek family tree hai: sabse upar Dada aur Dadi; unke neeche Papa aur Chacha; Papa ke neeche Anu. Anu ki dadi kaun hain? Bolo, phir unke box pe tap karo.
items.answer: Dadi (the box at the top next to Dada).
acceptable: the top box next to dada
hints: Start from Anu's box and move up.
Anu's papa is in the middle row — who is above him?
Papa's mother is Anu's ___.
Dadi — Papa's mother, at the top of the tree.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'A family must always have a mummy, a papa and two children — otherwise it is not a family.' Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Family mein hamesha mummy, papa aur do bachche hone chahiye — warna woh family nahi hai.' Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No. Families come in many kinds — with grandparents, with one parent, with many cousins, or with one child — and all are families.
acceptable: wrong, there are many kinds of families
galat hai, family alag-alag tarah ki hoti hai
hints: Think of families you know — are they all the same?
Remember Zoya with her nani and mother.
Families can be big, small, with one ___ or with grandparents.
It's wrong: every kind of family that cares for each other is a real family.

items.prompt_en: Mithu the baby parrot thinks only mummies do housework. Teach Mithu: who can help at home, and why is sharing good?
items.prompt_hi: Mithu tote ko lagta hai ki ghar ka kaam sirf mummy karti hai. Mithu ko samjhao — ghar mein kaun-kaun madad kar sakta hai, aur milke kaam karna achha kyun hai?
items.answer: Anyone — men, women, boys, girls, children and elders — can do housework; sharing gets the work done faster and nobody gets too tired.
acceptable: everyone can help, sharing makes work easier
sab madad kar sakte hain, kaam jaldi hota hai
hints: Who in a family could cook or clean?
What happens when the work is shared?
Tell Mithu: ___ can help, and sharing means ___.
Anyone can do housework, and sharing means work is quicker and no one is worn out.

items.prompt_en: Quick one from last time: tell me two different kinds of families.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar wali baat — do alag tarah ki families batao.
items.answer: Any two: a small family (parents and children), a joint family (grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins), a single-parent family, children living with grandparents.
hints: Think of the families we talked about.
Some were big, some were small.
One kind is a ___ family with grandparents, uncles and cousins.
For example, a small family and a joint family.

workedExample.problem: Rehana's family has five people: Dadi, Ammi, Abbu, Rehana (8) and her brother Imran (5). Plan who helps with the morning jobs.
steps: List the morning jobs: making breakfast, filling water bottles, packing school bags, watering plants.
Match each grown-up job to someone who can do it: Abbu makes breakfast, Ammi packs tiffins, Dadi waters the plants.
Give the children small jobs that suit their age: Rehana fills the bottles, Imran puts his own books in his bag.
Check: everyone has a share, so the work finishes on time and nobody gets too tired.
fadedVersion: List the morning jobs: making breakfast, filling bottles, packing bags, watering ___.
Match each grown-up job to someone who can ___ it.
Give the children small jobs that suit their ___.
Check: everyone has a share, so nobody gets too ___.

skills.title: Describe what good friends do for each other and how to play fairly
Recognise that animals have feelings and needs (food, water, shelter, gentle care)
Choose safe and kind ways to behave with pets and street animals

expectations: Friends share, take turns, help and include each other; a friend can be different from us in age, language or likes.
Animals feel hunger, thirst, pain, fear and happiness, just as we do.
Pets need food, clean water, shelter, gentle handling, play and rest — and someone responsible for them.
With street animals: stay calm, don't tease or rush at them, don't touch an unknown animal without an adult, and never disturb an animal that is eating or sleeping.

misconceptions.belief: Pets and other animals do not have feelings.
signs: Says 'dogs don't feel anything'
Laughs at teasing an animal or calls pulling a tail a game
Says animals 'just make noises'

diagnostic.prompt_en: A puppy's tail gets pulled hard. It yelps and runs away. What does that tell us?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek puppy ki poonch zor se kheenchi gayi. Woh chillaya aur bhaag gaya. Isse kya pata chalta hai?

options.text: The puppy felt pain and got scared
The puppy was playing a game
Animals can't feel pain; it was just a noise

remediation.representation: Animation of dog body language: loose wagging tail, tail tucked with ears back, teeth showing
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to match each body sign to a feeling, then link it to how they feel when they are hurt or scared

misconceptions.belief: Any friendly-looking street animal is safe to touch or hug straight away.
signs: Says 'I'll just go and hug it'
Runs towards unknown dogs or cows
Thinks a wagging tail always means 'come and pet me'

diagnostic.prompt_en: You see a street dog you don't know near your gate. What is the best thing to do?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tumhare gate ke paas ek anjaan street dog baitha hai. Sabse sahi kya karna chahiye?

options.text: Run up and hug it
Throw a stone so it goes away
Stay calm, don't touch it, and ask an adult before giving it water

remediation.representation: Traffic-light card: green = calm and at a distance, amber = ask an adult first, red = never (touch a sleeping or eating dog, tease, run at it)
remediation.moveShape: Contrast two scenes and ask which child is safer AND kinder, and why

misconceptions.belief: A friend has to be just like you — same age, same language, same games.
signs: Says 'he can't be my friend, he speaks a different language'
Says an older neighbour or grandparent cannot be a friend

diagnostic.prompt_en: Can someone who speaks a different language, or is much older, be your friend?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya koi jo doosri bhasha bolta hai, ya tumse bahut bada hai, tumhara dost ban sakta hai?

options.text: Yes — friends can be different from us
No — friends must be the same age
No — friends must like exactly the same games

remediation.representation: Story pair: two children with no common language become friends by playing ball together
remediation.moveShape: Ask what made them friends — the things they DID, not how alike they were

items.prompt_en: Tell me one thing a good friend does.
items.prompt_hi: Ek achha dost kya karta hai? Ek baat batao.
items.answer: Shares, takes turns, helps, plays fairly, includes others or cheers you up.
hints: Think of your best friend — what do they do that you like?
Think about games and sharing.
A good friend ___ things and takes ___.
A good friend shares, takes turns and helps.

items.prompt_en: Name three things a pet dog or cat needs every day.
items.prompt_hi: Ek pet kutte ya billi ko roz kya-kya chahiye? Teen cheezein batao.
items.answer: Food, clean water and a safe place to rest; also gentle care, play or a walk.
acceptable: khaana paani aur rehne ki jagah
hints: What do YOU need every day to stay well?
Think of eating, drinking and sleeping.
Food, clean ___ and a safe place to ___.
Food, clean water and a safe, shady place to rest.

items.prompt_en: Think first: a pet dog's family goes out all day on a hot summer day and forgets to leave water. How will the dog be by evening?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle socho: garmi ka din hai, family poore din bahar chali gayi aur kutte ke liye paani rakhna bhool gayi. Shaam tak kutta kaisa hoga?
items.answer: Very thirsty, tired and unhappy, panting a lot — animals need water, especially in heat.
hints: How do you feel after playing in the sun without water?
Dogs cool down by panting — that uses water.
The dog will be very ___ and ___.
It will be very thirsty and uncomfortable — it needs water all day.

items.prompt_en: Guess: a street dog is eating its food, and a child suddenly grabs the bowl. What might the dog do?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek street dog khaana kha raha hai, aur ek bachcha achanak uska bartan kheench leta hai. Kutta kya kar sakta hai?
items.answer: It might growl, snap or even bite, because it feels its food is being taken — so never disturb an animal while it eats.
hints: How would you feel if someone grabbed your plate?
Animals protect their food.
The dog may ___ or even ___.
It may growl or bite — never disturb an animal that is eating.

items.prompt_en: A cat purrs and rubs against your leg, but runs away when someone shouts. Why do you think it does both?
items.prompt_hi: Ek billi tumhare pair se lipat ke 'purr-purr' karti hai, par jab koi chillata hai toh bhaag jaati hai. Woh dono kyun karti hai?
items.answer: Because animals have feelings: the cat feels safe and happy with gentle people and gets scared by loud shouting.
acceptable: it feels happy and then scared
khush hoti hai aur phir darr jaati hai
hints: What might the cat be feeling when it purrs?
And what about when it hears shouting?
Purring shows it feels ___; running shows it feels ___.
The cat feels safe with gentle people and frightened by loud noise — animals have feelings.

items.prompt_en: Pinky keeps all the turns to herself when playing carrom. Sonu lets everyone take turns. Who is being a good friend, and what is the difference?
items.prompt_hi: Carrom khelte waqt Pinky saari baari khud le leti hai. Sonu sabko baari-baari khelne deta hai. Achha dost kaun hai, aur dono mein farak kya hai?
items.answer: Sonu. Taking turns is fair and lets everyone enjoy; keeping all the turns leaves others feeling left out.
hints: How would the others feel when playing with Pinky?
What does Sonu do that Pinky doesn't?
Sonu lets everyone take ___.
Sonu — sharing turns is fair, so everyone has fun.

items.prompt_en: A cow is standing in your lane on a very hot day. What is one kind and safe thing you could do, with an adult?
items.prompt_hi: Garmi ke din tumhari gali mein ek gaay khadi hai. Ek achha aur safe kaam batao jo tum kisi bade ke saath kar sakte ho.
items.answer: With an adult, put out a bucket or bowl of clean water, keep a safe distance, and never feed it plastic or tease it.
acceptable: put out water with an adult
bade ke saath paani rakh do
hints: What does every animal need most in the heat?
Remember to keep a safe distance.
With an adult, put out a bucket of clean ___.
Put out clean water with an adult's help and stay at a safe distance.

items.prompt_en: At a small zoo, a monkey is kept alone in a tiny cage with no branches to climb. Using what you know about animals' needs and feelings, what is wrong here?
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote zoo mein ek bandar akela ek tiny pinjre mein hai, chadhne ke liye koi daali nahi. Jaanwaron ki zarooraton aur feelings ke hisaab se, yahan kya galat hai?
items.answer: The monkey cannot move, climb or play and has no company; animals need space, things to do and shelter, so it may feel bored, sad or stressed.
acceptable: it has no space to climb or play
it will feel bored or sad
usko jagah aur khelne ko chahiye
hints: What does a monkey love to do?
Can it do that in a tiny cage?
It needs ___ to climb and others to be with.
It has no space, nothing to climb and no company — it will feel stressed and bored.

items.prompt_en: On the screen are three dogs: one with a loose, wagging tail; one with its tail tucked between its legs and ears flat; one showing its teeth. Tap the scared dog, and tell me which dogs you should not go near.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe teen kutte hain: ek ki poonch dheele se hil rahi hai; ek ki poonch pairon ke beech dabi hai aur kaan peeche; ek daant dikha raha hai. Darre hue kutte pe tap karo, aur batao kin kutton ke paas nahi jaana chahiye.
items.answer: The dog with its tail tucked and ears flat is scared. Don't go near the scared dog or the one showing its teeth.
acceptable: tail tucked is scared; stay away from scared and teeth-showing dogs
dabi poonch wala dara hua hai
hints: Look at the tails first.
A tucked tail and flat ears show worry.
Tucked tail = ___; teeth showing = stay ___.
Tucked tail means scared; avoid both the scared dog and the one showing teeth.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'If a street dog wags its tail it is always happy, so you can run up and hug it.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Agar street dog poonch hila raha hai, toh woh hamesha khush hai, toh daud ke usse gale laga lo.'
items.answer: That's wrong. A wagging tail can also mean excitement or nervousness; never rush at or hug an unknown dog — stay calm and ask an adult.
acceptable: wrong, wagging doesn't always mean happy
galat hai, anjaan kutte ko gale nahi lagaate
hints: Is a wagging tail the only sign to look at?
How might a dog feel if a stranger runs at it?
Wagging can mean ___ too, and you should never ___ an unknown dog.
Wrong — wagging isn't always happy; stay calm and ask an adult first.

items.prompt_en: Mithu the parrot is getting a puppy and thinks a puppy is like a toy. Teach Mithu how to look after it, and why.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu tota ek puppy laane wala hai aur sochta hai ki puppy ek khilona hai. Mithu ko samjhao puppy ka dhyaan kaise rakhein, aur kyun.
items.answer: A puppy is alive and has feelings; it needs food, clean water, shelter, gentle handling, play and rest; it feels pain and fear, so never hurt or tease it.
acceptable: puppy is alive and has feelings; needs food, water, shelter and gentle care
hints: Is a puppy like a toy? What's different?
List what it needs every day.
A puppy feels ___, and needs food, ___ and a safe place.
It's alive and has feelings — it needs food, water, shelter, play and gentle care.

items.prompt_en: From last time: tell me one way to be a good friend, and one thing every pet needs.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar humne kya seekha tha? Achha dost banne ka ek tareeka batao, aur ek cheez jo har pet ko chahiye.
items.answer: A way to be a good friend (share, take turns, help) and one pet need (food, clean water, shelter, gentle care).
hints: Think of carrom and the thirsty dog.
One answer is about friends, one about pets.
A friend takes ___; a pet needs clean ___.
For example: take turns, and give clean water.

workedExample.problem: A thirsty street puppy is sitting in the hot sun near your building. Plan how to help it safely.
steps: Stop and stay calm — don't run at it or touch it.
Tell an adult at home what you saw.
With the adult, put a shallow bowl of clean water in the shade near the puppy and step back.
Watch from a distance; if the puppy looks hurt, the adult can call a local animal helpline.
fadedVersion: Stop and stay ___ — don't run at it or touch it.
Tell an ___ at home what you saw.
With the adult, put a bowl of clean ___ in the shade and step back.
Watch from a ___; if it looks hurt, the adult calls for help.

skills.title: Describe the stalls, rides, food and activities at a mela or haat
Identify the many people who work at a mela (sellers, cooks, artisans, ride operators, performers, cleaners, police)
Explain where things sold at a mela come from and how they get there

expectations: A mela or haat is a gathering where people buy, sell, eat, play and meet.
Many kinds of people work there: sellers, cooks, artisans, farmers, ride operators, performers, cleaners, police and volunteers.
Things sold at a mela were made or grown somewhere else — on farms, in workshops, in artisans' homes — and carried there by cart, tempo, truck, camel or on heads.
Some melas are also for trade, like buying and selling camels and cattle at the Pushkar fair.

misconceptions.belief: Only shopkeepers work at a mela.
signs: Lists only sellers when asked who works there
Says the police or cleaners are 'just visiting'
Thinks the giant wheel runs by itself

diagnostic.prompt_en: Who is working at a mela?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Mele mein kaun-kaun kaam kar raha hota hai?

options.text: Only the people selling things
Sellers, cooks, ride operators, cleaners, police and performers
Nobody — everyone is there just for fun

remediation.representation: Busy mela scene where each worker lights up when tapped, with a one-word job label
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to find one more worker each time, then ask what would go wrong without that person

misconceptions.belief: Things at the mela just appear there, or are made at the stall itself.
signs: Says 'the bangles come from the stall'
Cannot say where vegetables at a haat were grown

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where did the clay pots at the mela stall come from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Mele ki dukaan pe jo mitti ke bartan hain, woh kahaan se aaye?

options.text: A potter made them earlier and brought them to the mela
They grow at the mela
The stall itself is where pots are always made

remediation.representation: Journey-map animation: farm or workshop → cart or tempo → mela stall
remediation.moveShape: Trace backwards: keep asking 'and before the stall?' until the child reaches the maker or the farm

misconceptions.belief: A mela is only for fun; nobody there is working or earning.
signs: Says the balloon man is 'playing'
Doesn't count performers or ride operators as working

diagnostic.prompt_en: A magician does tricks at the mela all day. Is he playing or working?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek jaadugar poore din mele mein jaadu dikhata hai. Woh khel raha hai ya kaam kar raha hai?

options.text: Working — he earns money by performing
Just playing for fun

remediation.representation: Two-column sort, 'having fun' and 'working', where some people fit both (a juggler enjoys it AND earns)
remediation.moveShape: Ask who gets paid and why; resolve that fun and work can overlap

items.prompt_en: Name three things you can see or do at a mela.
items.prompt_hi: Mele mein kya-kya dikhta hai ya kya kar sakte hain? Teen cheezein batao.
items.answer: Any three, e.g. giant wheel or jhoola, food stalls, bangles and toys, balloons, a magic or puppet show.
hints: Close your eyes and imagine walking into a mela.
What do you hear, see, smell, ride?
There are rides like the ___ and stalls selling ___.
For example: the giant wheel, a food stall and a bangle stall.

items.prompt_en: Name four people who are working at a mela — not just shopkeepers.
items.prompt_hi: Mele mein kaam karne wale chaar log batao — sirf dukaandaar nahi.
items.answer: Any four, e.g. ride operator, cook or halwai, balloon seller, cleaner, police officer, puppeteer, juggler, farmer selling vegetables, ticket seller.
acceptable: jhoola chalane wala, halwai, safai wala, police
hints: Who makes the giant wheel go round?
Who keeps the ground clean and the crowd safe?
Think of the ___ operator, the cook, the ___ and the police.
