Think of til and gud.
In winter there's ___, when we eat ___.
For example, Makar Sankranti with til-gud laddoos.

items.prompt_en: Imagine a village where the mango trees give a big crop in summer. If the village made a festival to celebrate it, which season would it be in, and what might they cook?
items.prompt_hi: Socho ek gaon hai jahaan garmi mein aam ki badi fasal aati hai. Agar woh gaon iska tyohaar banaaye, toh woh kis season mein hoga, aur kya pakaayenge?
items.answer: Summer, at mango time; something made with mangoes, like aamras or aam panna.
acceptable: garmi mein, aam se bani cheezein
hints: When are the mangoes ready?
Harvest festivals come right after the crop is ready.
It would be in ___, with food made from ___.
Summer — with dishes like aamras made from the new mangoes.

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a map of India with empty boxes on Punjab, Assam, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Drag the festival names — Baisakhi, Bihu, Pongal, Onam — to the right states.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe India ka map hai, Punjab, Assam, Tamil Nadu aur Kerala pe khaali box hain. Baisakhi, Bihu, Pongal aur Onam ko sahi state pe drag karo.
items.answer: Punjab — Baisakhi; Assam — Bihu; Tamil Nadu — Pongal; Kerala — Onam.
acceptable: punjab baisakhi, assam bihu, tamil nadu pongal, kerala onam
hints: Start with the one you're surest about.
Bihu goes in the north-east.
Kerala is in the far south-west — it gets ___.
Punjab–Baisakhi, Assam–Bihu, Tamil Nadu–Pongal, Kerala–Onam.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'Onam is a festival of Punjab, where people make flower carpets.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Onam Punjab ka tyohaar hai, jahaan log phoolon ka kaaleen banaate hain.'
items.answer: Onam is from Kerala (the flower carpet is the pookalam); Punjab's harvest festivals are Baisakhi and Lohri.
acceptable: onam kerala ka hai, punjab ka nahi
hints: Which state is Onam really from?
Which festivals belong to Punjab?
Onam is from ___; Punjab has ___.
Onam belongs to Kerala; Punjab celebrates Baisakhi and Lohri.

items.prompt_en: Mithu thinks festivals happen on random days. Teach Mithu why harvest festivals come at a special time, and how different states celebrate them.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu ko lagta hai tyohaar kisi bhi din ho jaate hain. Mithu ko samjhao ki harvest festivals ek khaas waqt pe kyun aate hain, aur alag states unhe kaise manaate hain.
items.answer: Harvest festivals come when the crop is ready (e.g. Baisakhi with wheat in April, Pongal with rice in January); each state has its own festival, food and dances, like Onam, Bihu and Pongal.
acceptable: they come when crops are ready; each state celebrates differently
hints: What has to happen before a harvest festival?
Give Mithu two examples from different states.
They come when the ___ is ready, and each state has its own ___.
They follow the harvest, and every state has its own festival, food and dance.

items.prompt_en: From last time: Bihu is celebrated in which state?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ki baat: Bihu kis state mein manaaya jaata hai?
items.answer: Assam.
hints: It's in the north-east of India.
Famous for tea gardens.
Bihu belongs to ___.
Assam.

workedExample.problem: Find out why Pongal is celebrated in mid-January in Tamil Nadu.
steps: Ask what the festival dish is made from: sweet pongal is made with new rice, jaggery and milk.
Ask when that rice is harvested in Tamil Nadu: around December–January.
Connect: the festival comes right after the harvest, as a thank-you for the crop, the sun and the cattle that help farmers.
Check with another festival: Baisakhi comes in April, when wheat is harvested in Punjab — the same pattern.
fadedVersion: The dish is made with new ___, jaggery and milk.
That rice is harvested around December–___.
The festival comes right after the ___ as a thank-you.
Baisakhi follows the ___ harvest in Punjab — the same pattern.

skills.title: Read traffic lights and pedestrian signals (red, amber, green; walking and standing person)
Use zebra crossings and the look right–left–right rule safely
Recognise common symbols (hospital, no horn, school ahead, recycle, danger) and what they ask us to do

expectations: Red means stop, amber (yellow) means get ready to stop, green means go; for walkers, a green walking person means you may cross and a red standing person means wait.
Cross at a zebra crossing, but still stop, look right, left and right again (in India vehicles keep to the left, so the nearest traffic comes from your right), and walk — don't run.
Signs and symbols use pictures so that people of any language, even those who cannot read, understand them quickly.
Signs are for everyone — walkers, cyclists and children — not only drivers.

misconceptions.belief: Signs and signals are only for drivers.
signs: Says 'I don't need signals, I'm walking'
Ignores the pedestrian light
Thinks children don't need to know signs

diagnostic.prompt_en: Who should obey the walking-person signal at a crossing?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Crossing pe chalte hue insaan wala signal kisko maanna chahiye?

options.text: People walking — including children
Only car and bus drivers

remediation.representation: Street-scene animation with a vehicle signal and a walkers' signal side by side
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to find which signal is 'talking' to them, and what it says

misconceptions.belief: A green signal or a zebra crossing means it is safe to run across without looking.
signs: Says 'green means run fast'
Says 'cars always stop at the zebra'

diagnostic.prompt_en: The walking-person light turns green. What should you do?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Chalne wale insaan ki batti green ho gayi. Ab kya karna chahiye?

options.text: Look right, left and right again, then walk across
Run across without looking — green means safe
Wait until it turns red, then cross

remediation.representation: Animation where a late bike rushes through just after the signal turns, and a child who looked stays safe
remediation.moveShape: Contrast the child who looked with the one who ran; ask what looking added

misconceptions.belief: An amber (yellow) light means go faster to beat the red.
signs: Says 'yellow means hurry'
Cheers when a car speeds through on amber

diagnostic.prompt_en: The traffic light for cars turns amber (yellow). What is it telling the driver?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Gaadiyon ki batti peeli (amber) ho gayi. Yeh driver ko kya bol rahi hai?

options.text: Get ready to stop
Go faster before it turns red

remediation.representation: Three-light sequence cards with a 'slow down' arrow on amber
remediation.moveShape: Ask what would happen at the crossing if every driver sped up on amber

items.prompt_en: What do the three traffic-light colours tell vehicles?
items.prompt_hi: Traffic light ke teen rang gaadiyon ko kya batate hain?
items.answer: Red: stop. Amber or yellow: get ready to stop. Green: go.
acceptable: red stop, yellow get ready, green go
laal ruko, peela taiyaar, hara chalo
hints: Start with the top light.
Which colour means danger, which means go?
Red means ___, green means ___.
Red stop, amber get ready to stop, green go.

items.prompt_en: What does a red plus sign on a building or signboard usually mean?
items.prompt_hi: Kisi building ya board pe laal plus (+) ka nishaan ho, toh aam taur pe uska kya matlab hota hai?
items.answer: A hospital, clinic or first aid — medical help is here.
hints: Where do you go when you are hurt or ill?
Think of an ambulance.
It shows a ___ or first aid.
It means a hospital or first-aid point.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: in India, vehicles keep to the LEFT side of the road. When you step off the footpath to cross, from which side will the nearest vehicles come?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: India mein gaadiyan sadak ke BAAYIN (left) taraf chalti hain. Jab tum footpath se sadak paar karne utarte ho, toh sabse paas wali gaadiyan kis taraf se aayengi?
items.answer: From the right — that is why we look right first.
hints: Picture standing at the edge of the road, facing across.
Cars keep left — which lane is closest to you?
The nearest cars come from your ___.
From the right, so we look right first.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if a busy crossing had no traffic lights and no zebra crossing, what would happen when lots of people and vehicles arrived at once?
items.prompt_hi: Socho: agar ek busy chauraahe pe na traffic light ho na zebra crossing, toh jab bahut saare log aur gaadiyan ek saath aayein toh kya hoga?
items.answer: Confusion and jams, and accidents become more likely — signals tell everyone when to stop and go so they take turns safely.
acceptable: sab ek saath chalenge aur accident hoga
hints: Who would decide who goes first?
What happens when everyone goes at once?
There would be ___ and more ___.
Chaos and accidents — signals help everyone take turns.

items.prompt_en: Why do so many road signs use pictures instead of only words?
items.prompt_hi: Itne saare road signs mein sirf shabd ki jagah tasveerein kyun hoti hain?
items.answer: So that people who speak different languages, or cannot read, can understand quickly, even from far away.
acceptable: people who can't read can also understand
hints: Would a sign in one language work for everyone?
How fast can a driver read while moving?
Pictures can be understood by ___, quickly.
Pictures work for every language and reader, and are quick to see.

items.prompt_en: At one crossing, the walkers' signal shows a red standing person while the cars' signal shows green. Who is each signal for, and what should you do?
items.prompt_hi: Ek crossing pe chalne walon ka signal laal khada insaan dikha raha hai, aur gaadiyon ka signal hara hai. Kaunsa signal kiske liye hai, aur tumhe kya karna chahiye?
items.answer: The red standing person is for walkers — wait; the green is for vehicles — they are moving, so you must not cross.
acceptable: red man is for me so I wait; green is for cars
laal insaan mere liye hai, main rukunga
hints: Which signal has a person on it?
If cars have green, are they moving?
The person signal is for ___; I must ___.
Walkers' red means wait; cars' green means they're moving — don't cross.

items.prompt_en: Near a hospital you see a sign with a horn crossed out. What is it asking drivers to do, and why there?
items.prompt_hi: Hospital ke paas ek sign hai jisme horn ke upar cross bana hai. Yeh drivers se kya keh raha hai, aur wahan kyun?
items.answer: Don't honk — patients need quiet to rest and get better.
acceptable: horn mat bajao, mareezon ko aaraam chahiye
hints: What does a cross over a picture usually mean?
Who is inside a hospital?
It means no ___, because patients need ___.
No honking — the patients need quiet.

items.prompt_en: You and your elder sister have to cross a road with no zebra crossing and no signal. Using what you know, how should you cross safely?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhe aur tumhari badi didi ko aisi sadak paar karni hai jahaan na zebra crossing hai na signal. Jo seekha hai uske hisaab se, safe tareeke se kaise paar karoge?
items.answer: Hold the adult's hand; choose a spot where you can see clearly (not between parked cars or at a bend); stop at the edge; look right, left and right again; cross straight across when clear; walk, don't run.
acceptable: hold hands, find a clear spot, look right left right, walk straight
haath pakdo, right-left-right dekho, seedha chalo
hints: Where can you see traffic best?
What's the looking rule?
Find a clear spot, look ___-___-___, and walk.
Hold hands, pick a clear spot, look right-left-right, then walk straight across.

items.prompt_en: On the screen are four symbols: recycling arrows, a skull and crossbones, a red triangle with two children walking, and a crossed-out horn. Match each to its meaning: 'school ahead', 'danger or poison', 'no honking', 'can be recycled'.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe chaar nishaan hain: recycling wale teer, khopdi aur haddiyaan, do bachchon wala laal triangle, aur cross wala horn. Har ek ko uske matlab se milaao: 'aage school hai', 'khatra ya zeher', 'horn mana hai', 'recycle ho sakta hai'.
items.answer: Recycling arrows — can be recycled; skull and crossbones — danger or poison; triangle with children — school ahead; crossed-out horn — no honking.
acceptable: arrows recycle, skull danger, children school, horn no honking
hints: Which one looks scary? That's a warning.
Which one shows kids?
Children in a triangle means ___ ahead.
Arrows–recycle, skull–danger, children–school ahead, crossed horn–no honking.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'When the traffic light turns yellow, the driver should speed up to cross before it goes red.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Jab batti peeli ho jaaye, toh driver ko tez chala ke red hone se pehle nikal jaana chahiye.'
items.answer: Wrong. Amber (yellow) means get ready to stop; speeding up is dangerous for walkers and other vehicles.
acceptable: wrong, yellow means get ready to stop
galat, peela matlab rukne ki taiyaari
hints: What comes right after yellow?
Who might be starting to cross?
Amber means get ready to ___.
Wrong — amber means slow down and get ready to stop.

items.prompt_en: Mithu is crossing a road for the first time. Teach Mithu how to use the signal and the zebra crossing safely.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu pehli baar sadak paar kar raha hai. Mithu ko sikhao ki signal aur zebra crossing ka safe istemaal kaise karein.
items.answer: Wait at the edge; cross only on the green walking person; even then look right, left and right again; walk straight across on the zebra stripes without running; signals are for walkers too.
acceptable: wait for green person, look right left right, walk on zebra
hints: Where should Mithu wait?
What should Mithu check before stepping out, even on green?
Wait for the green ___, look ___-left-right, walk on the ___.
Wait for the green walking person, look right-left-right, and walk on the zebra.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what does a red standing person on a crossing signal tell you?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar wala sawaal: crossing ke signal pe laal khada insaan tumhe kya batata hai?
items.answer: Stop and wait — don't cross.
hints: Red usually means…?
The person is standing still, not walking.
It means ___ and don't cross.
Wait — do not cross yet.

workedExample.problem: Cross the road to school at a crossing with zebra stripes and a walking-person signal.
steps: Stop at the edge of the footpath, holding an adult's hand.
Check the walkers' signal: a red standing person means wait; wait for the green walking person.
When it turns green, still look right, then left, then right again to be sure vehicles have stopped.
Walk straight across on the zebra stripes — don't run, and don't stop in the middle.
fadedVersion: Stop at the ___ of the footpath, holding an adult's hand.
A red standing person means ___; wait for the green walking person.
Even on green, look right, then ___, then right again.
Walk straight across on the ___ stripes.

skills.title: Identify roots, stem, leaves, flowers and fruits on real plants
Say what each part does: roots hold and take in water, stem holds up and carries water, leaves make food using sunlight, flowers become fruits with seeds
Recognise variations: roots above ground (banyan, money plant) and plants that never flower (ferns, mosses)

expectations: Most plants have roots, a stem and leaves; many also have flowers, which turn into fruits with seeds inside.
Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil and take in water (with a few minerals) from it.
The stem holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.
Leaves make the plant's food using sunlight, air and water — plants do not eat soil.
Some roots grow above the ground, like the banyan's hanging roots, and some plants, like ferns and mosses, never have flowers.

misconceptions.belief: Plants get their food from the soil — roots 'eat' soil or manure.
signs: Says 'the roots eat the soil'
Says khaad (manure) is the plant's food
Expects the soil in a pot to get used up as the plant grows

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where does a mango tree get its food from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Aam ke ped ko apna khaana kahaan se milta hai?

options.text: It makes its own food in its leaves, using sunlight, air and water
It eats soil through its roots
It eats the manure that is put around it

remediation.representation: Pot-and-scale story: a small plant grows into a big one over years, yet the soil in the pot barely goes down
remediation.moveShape: Predict-observe-explain: ask how much soil will be gone, reveal that almost none is, then ask where the plant's body came from — leading to leaves and sunlight

misconceptions.belief: All plants have flowers and fruits.
signs: Says 'every plant gets flowers if you wait'
Is puzzled by a fern or moss
Calls fern spore dots 'seeds'

diagnostic.prompt_en: Does every plant make flowers?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya har paudhe pe phool aate hain?

options.text: No — some plants, like ferns and mosses, never have flowers
Yes, every plant gets flowers if you wait long enough

remediation.representation: Photo pair: a fern with spore dots under its leaves next to a flowering hibiscus
remediation.moveShape: Contrasting cases: check each plant against the parts list, and notice which part the fern never has

misconceptions.belief: Roots are always underground.
signs: Calls the banyan's hanging strands ropes, hair or branches
Says 'roots can't be in the air'

diagnostic.prompt_en: The long brown strands hanging from a banyan tree's branches — what are they?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bargad ke ped ki daaliyon se jo lambe bhoore dhaage latakte hain — woh kya hain?

options.text: Roots that grow in the air (aerial roots)
Branches that are falling down
Ropes that people tied

remediation.representation: Photo sequence of a banyan aerial root growing down, reaching the soil and thickening into a pillar
remediation.moveShape: Contrasting cases: carrot root versus banyan aerial root — ask what job both do (hold the plant, take in water)

items.prompt_en: Name the parts of a tulsi plant, starting from the soil and going up.
items.prompt_hi: Tulsi ke paudhe ke hisse batao — neeche mitti se shuru karke upar tak.
items.answer: Roots, stem, leaves, and on top the small flower spikes (manjari) that make seeds.
hints: What part is hidden in the soil?
What holds the leaves up?
From the bottom: ___, stem, ___, flowers.
Roots, stem, leaves and the flower spikes (manjari).

items.prompt_en: What do roots do for a plant? Tell me two jobs.
items.prompt_hi: Jadein paudhe ke liye kya karti hain? Do kaam batao.
items.answer: They hold the plant firmly in the soil, and they take in water (and some minerals) from the soil.
acceptable: hold the plant and take water
paudhe ko pakad ke rakhti hain aur paani leti hain
hints: What would happen to a plant with no roots in a strong wind?
And how does water get into the plant?
Roots ___ the plant and take in ___.
They hold the plant in place and soak up water from the soil.

items.prompt_en: Think first, then I'll tell you. A small plant is put in a big pot of soil and, over many years, grows into a big plant. Will the soil in the pot be almost all gone, or nearly the same?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle socho, phir main bataungi. Ek chhota paudha mitti bhare bade gamle mein lagaya, aur kai saalon mein woh bada ho gaya. Gamle ki mitti lagbhag khatam ho jaayegi, ya utni hi rahegi?
items.answer: Nearly the same. The plant did not eat the soil; it made its food in its leaves using sunlight, air and water.
hints: If the plant ate soil, what would happen to the pot?
Long ago someone weighed the soil after five years — it had barely changed.
The soil stays nearly the ___, because food is made in the ___.
Nearly the same — the plant's food comes from its leaves, sunlight, air and water.

items.prompt_en: Try this at home with an adult: keep one small potted plant in a dark cupboard and one by a sunny window for a week, watering both the same. Before you look — what will happen to the plant in the dark? (Then bring it back into the light.)
items.prompt_hi: Ghar pe kisi bade ke saath try karo: ek chhota gamla ek hafte andhere almaari mein rakho aur ek dhoop wali khidki ke paas, dono ko barabar paani do. Dekhne se pehle batao — andhere wale paudhe ka kya hoga? (Baad mein usse wapas roshni mein rakh dena.)
items.answer: Its leaves will turn pale or yellowish and it will look weak and droopy, because leaves need sunlight to make food.
hints: What do leaves need to make food?
Is there any light in the cupboard?
Without sunlight the leaves turn ___ and the plant gets ___.
The leaves go pale or yellow and the plant weakens — no light, no food.

items.prompt_en: With an adult, put a white flower (like a white rose or sevanti) in a glass of water with a few drops of food colouring. Guess first: what will the petals look like tomorrow?
items.prompt_hi: Kisi bade ke saath, ek safed phool (jaise safed gulaab ya sevanti) ko ek glass paani mein rakho jisme thoda food colour mila ho. Pehle guess karo: kal tak pankhudiyaan kaisi dikhengi?
items.answer: The petals will get a little coloured, because the stem carries the coloured water up to the flower.
hints: Where does the water in the glass go?
Which part carries water up the plant?
The stem carries the coloured ___ up, so the petals get ___.
They turn slightly coloured — the stem carried the water up to them.

items.prompt_en: You said leaves make the plant's food. Why do you think most leaves are flat and spread out?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha patte paudhe ka khaana banaate hain. Toh zyaadatar patte chapte aur faile hue kyun hote hain?
items.answer: To catch as much sunlight as possible, which they need to make food.
hints: What does a leaf need from the sky?
Would a flat sheet or a ball catch more light?
A flat leaf catches more ___.
Flat, spread-out leaves catch more sunlight for making food.

items.prompt_en: A carrot root and a banyan's hanging root look very different — one is under the soil, one hangs in the air. What job do both do?
items.prompt_hi: Gaajar ki jad aur bargad ki latakti jad bilkul alag dikhti hain — ek mitti ke andar, ek hawa mein. Dono ka kaam kya hai?
items.answer: Both are roots: they help hold the plant up and take in water. The banyan's root grows down into the soil and becomes a pillar that supports the branches.
acceptable: both hold the plant and take in water
dono jad hain, sahara dete hain aur paani lete hain
hints: What do all roots do?
What happens when a banyan root reaches the ground?
Both ___ the plant and take in ___.
Both are roots — they support the plant and take in water.

items.prompt_en: You find a plant on a damp wall with feathery leaves and little brown dots under the leaves, but no flowers at all. Can it still be a plant?
items.prompt_hi: Ek geeli deewar pe tumhe ek paudha milta hai — pankh jaise patte, patton ke neeche chhote bhoore dots, par phool bilkul nahi. Kya yeh phir bhi paudha hai?
items.answer: Yes. It is probably a fern — ferns have roots, stems and leaves but never flowers; the brown dots make spores, which grow into new ferns.
acceptable: yes, some plants have no flowers
hints: Does it have roots, a stem and leaves?
Do all plants need flowers?
Yes — it's a ___, a plant without ___.
Yes, it's a fern; ferns are plants that never flower.

items.prompt_en: Which part of the plant are we eating when we eat a carrot, spinach, a cauliflower and peas?
items.prompt_hi: Jab hum gaajar, paalak, phoolgobhi aur matar khaate hain, toh paudhe ka kaunsa hissa kha rahe hote hain?
items.answer: Carrot — root; spinach — leaf; cauliflower — flower; peas — seed.
hints: Which one grows under the soil?
Cauliflower's name has a clue in it.
Carrot is a ___, cauliflower is a ___.
Carrot root, spinach leaf, cauliflower flower, peas seed.

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a drawing of a hibiscus plant with five empty labels. Drag the words root, stem, leaf, flower and bud to the right places, then tell me which part is under the soil.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe gudhal ke paudhe ki drawing hai, paanch khaali labels ke saath. Root, stem, leaf, flower aur bud ko sahi jagah drag karo, phir batao kaunsa hissa mitti ke neeche hai.
items.answer: Roots under the soil; the stem is the upright woody part; leaves are the flat green parts; the flower is the big red part; the bud is the closed young flower. The roots are under the soil.
hints: Start with the part you can't see above ground.
A bud is a flower that hasn't opened yet.
Under the soil are the ___.
Roots below, stem up the middle, leaves, flower, and a closed bud — roots are underground.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'Plants eat soil through their roots — soil is their food.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Paudhe jadon se mitti khaate hain — mitti hi unka khaana hai.'
items.answer: Wrong. Roots take in water and a few minerals from the soil, but the plant makes its own food in its leaves using sunlight, air and water.
hints: Remember the pot whose soil barely went down.
Which part makes food, and with what?
Roots take ___; the food is made in the ___.
Wrong — leaves make the food from sunlight, air and water; roots only take in water and minerals.

items.prompt_en: Mithu has never looked closely at a plant. Teach Mithu the parts of a plant and the job of each part.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu ne kabhi paudhe ko dhyaan se nahi dekha. Mithu ko paudhe ke hisse aur har hisse ka kaam samjhao.
items.answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water; the stem holds it up and carries water; leaves make food using sunlight, air and water; flowers turn into fruits with seeds. Some roots grow in the air and some plants never flower.
acceptable: roots take water, stem carries it, leaves make food, flowers make fruits
hints: Start from the bottom of the plant.
For each part, say one job.
Roots take ___, stem ___ it, leaves make ___.
Roots absorb water, the stem carries it, leaves make food, flowers become fruits and seeds.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what are the long brown strands that hang down from a banyan tree?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ka sawaal: bargad ke ped se jo lambe bhoore dhaage latakte hain, woh kya hain?
items.answer: Aerial roots — roots that grow in the air.
hints: They grow downwards towards the soil.
Are they branches or something else?
They are ___ that grow in the air.
Aerial roots.

workedExample.problem: Name the parts of a coriander (dhaniya) bunch from the market that still has its roots.
steps: Start at the bottom: the thin, pale, thread-like parts that were in the soil are the roots.
Above them, the thin upright green part that holds everything up is the stem.
The flat green parts on the stem are the leaves, which made the plant's food using sunlight.
Ask whether there are flowers or seeds: dhaniya seeds form after the plant flowers, so this plant can flower too.
fadedVersion: At the bottom, the thread-like parts from the soil are the ___.
The upright green part that holds the plant up is the ___.
The flat green parts that make food using sunlight are the ___.
Dhaniya seeds form after the plant makes ___.

skills.title: Group plants as herbs, shrubs and trees by size and stem (soft green stem; several woody stems near the base; one thick woody trunk)
Tell climbers from creepers (weak stems that climb a support versus spread on the ground)
Observe and describe leaves by shape, size, smell and texture

expectations: Herbs are small plants with soft, green stems (wheat, coriander, grass, tomato).
Shrubs are bushy, medium-sized plants with several hard, woody stems near the ground (rose, hibiscus, mehendi).
Trees are tall plants with one thick, hard, woody trunk (mango, neem, peepal).
Climbers and creepers have weak stems: climbers climb up a support (money plant, grape, bitter gourd); creepers spread along the ground (pumpkin, watermelon).
Grass and trees are plants too, and leaves differ in shape, size, smell and feel.

misconceptions.belief: Grass is not a plant.
signs: Says 'grass is just grass'
Leaves grass out when sorting plants
Says grass has no roots or flowers

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is the grass on a lawn a plant?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya maidan ki ghaas ek paudha hai?

options.text: Yes — it has roots, a stem and leaves; it is a small herb
No — plants have to be bigger than that
No — grass doesn't have roots

remediation.representation: Magnified photo of a single grass plant pulled up, showing its roots, stem, leaves and tiny flowers
remediation.moveShape: Check the plant-parts list against the grass one part at a time

misconceptions.belief: Trees are not plants — a 'plant' means something small and green.
signs: Says 'a plant is small, a tree is a tree'
Sorts a mango tree outside the 'plants' group

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is a neem tree a plant?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya neem ka ped ek paudha hai?

options.text: Yes — a tree is a big plant with a woody trunk
No — only small things in pots are plants

remediation.representation: Nested circles: a big 'plants' circle containing herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers
remediation.moveShape: Ask what a neem and a tulsi both have (roots, stem, leaves), then place both inside the plant circle

misconceptions.belief: Climbers and creepers are baby trees, or climbers and creepers are the same thing.
signs: Says 'the money plant will grow into a tree'
Calls a pumpkin plant a climber

diagnostic.prompt_en: A pumpkin plant spreads along the ground, and a money plant goes up a wall. What are they?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaddu ka paudha zameen pe failta hai, aur money plant deewar pe chadhta hai. Yeh kya hain?

options.text: The pumpkin is a creeper; the money plant is a climber
Both are baby trees
Both are climbers

remediation.representation: Side-by-side animation: a weak stem with a support goes up; without a support it spreads along the ground
remediation.moveShape: Contrast: ask what each plant would do if there were no wall

items.prompt_en: Sort these: wheat, rose, mango. Which is a herb, which a shrub, which a tree?
items.prompt_hi: In teeno ko sort karo: gehun, gulaab, aam. Kaunsa herb hai, kaunsa shrub (jhaadi), kaunsa ped?
items.answer: Wheat — herb; rose — shrub; mango — tree.
acceptable: wheat herb, rose shrub, mango tree
gehun herb, gulaab jhaadi, aam ped
hints: Which is smallest with a soft stem?
Which is tall with one trunk?
Wheat is a ___, mango is a ___.
Wheat herb, rose shrub, mango tree.

items.prompt_en: How can you tell a shrub from a tree just by looking at its stem?
items.prompt_hi: Sirf tana dekh ke shrub aur ped mein farak kaise pata karoge?
items.answer: A shrub has several woody stems branching from near the ground and is bushy and medium-sized; a tree has one thick woody trunk and is tall.
acceptable: shrub has many stems, tree has one trunk
jhaadi ke kai tane, ped ka ek mota tana
hints: Count the stems coming out of the ground.
How thick is a tree's trunk?
A shrub has ___ stems; a tree has ___ thick trunk.
Several woody stems means shrub; one thick trunk means tree.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: if a money plant has no stick or wall to climb, what will it do as it grows longer?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: agar money plant ke paas chadhne ke liye na danda ho na deewar, toh lamba hote hue woh kya karega?
items.answer: It cannot stand up by itself, so it will hang down or spread along the floor, because its stem is weak.
acceptable: it will hang down or spread on the floor
neeche latak jayega ya zameen pe failega
hints: Is a money plant's stem strong or weak?
What does it normally hold on to?
Without support it will ___ or spread on the ___.
It flops down or trails along the floor — a weak stem needs support to climb.

items.prompt_en: Predict before you try: if you gently press the stem of a coriander plant and the stem of a hibiscus bush between two fingers, which will feel soft and which hard?
items.prompt_hi: Try karne se pehle socho: agar dhaniya ke paudhe ka tana aur gudhal ki jhaadi ka tana do ungliyon se halke se dabao, toh kaunsa naram lagega aur kaunsa sakht?
items.answer: Coriander's stem will feel soft and green (a herb); hibiscus will feel hard and woody (a shrub).
hints: Which plant is small and tender?
Which one is bushy with woody stems?
Coriander feels ___; hibiscus feels ___.
Coriander is soft (herb); hibiscus is hard and woody (shrub).

items.prompt_en: Before you smell them: if you gently rub a mint (pudina) leaf and a hibiscus leaf between your fingers, which will smell stronger? (Smell only — don't taste leaves you don't know.)
items.prompt_hi: Soonghne se pehle socho: agar pudina ka patta aur gudhal ka patta ungliyon mein halke se ragdo, toh kiski khushboo zyada tez hogi? (Sirf soongho — anjaan patte chakhna nahi.)
items.answer: The mint leaf has a strong smell; the hibiscus leaf has very little smell.
hints: Which leaf do we put in chutney for its smell?
Does a hibiscus leaf have a smell you know?
The ___ leaf smells much stronger.
Mint — it has a strong smell; hibiscus barely smells at all.

items.prompt_en: You said a neem is a tree. Why is it still called a plant?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha neem ek ped hai. Phir bhi use paudha kyun kehte hain?
items.answer: Because it has roots, a stem and leaves and it grows — a tree is just a big plant with a woody trunk.
acceptable: it has roots stem and leaves
hints: What parts does a tulsi plant have?
Does a neem have the same parts?
It has roots, a stem and ___, so it's a ___.
It has roots, a stem and leaves — a tree is simply a big plant.

items.prompt_en: Bitter gourd (karela) and watermelon both have weak stems. One climbs up a fence, the other spreads on the ground. Which is the climber and which is the creeper, and what is the key difference?
items.prompt_hi: Karela aur tarbooz — dono ke tane kamzor hain. Ek baad pe chadhta hai, doosra zameen pe failta hai. Kaunsa climber hai, kaunsa creeper, aur asli farak kya hai?
items.answer: Karela is the climber (it uses curly tendrils to climb a support); watermelon is the creeper (it spreads along the ground). The difference is whether it climbs up a support.
acceptable: karela chadhta hai, tarbooz failta hai
hints: Which one do you see on fences?
Which one lies on the ground with big fruits?
The climber goes ___ a support; the creeper spreads on the ___.
Karela climbs (climber); watermelon spreads on the ground (creeper).

items.prompt_en: On your way to school you see a plant about as tall as you, bushy, with lots of thin woody stems coming from the ground and big red flowers. Herb, shrub or tree?
items.prompt_hi: School jaate hue tum ek paudha dekhte ho — tumhari height jitna, ghana, zameen se kai patle sakht tane nikle hue, aur bade laal phool. Herb, shrub ya ped?
items.answer: A shrub (it could be a hibiscus).
hints: How tall is it, and how many stems?
Are the stems soft or woody?
Many woody stems from the ground means a ___.
A shrub — like a hibiscus.

items.prompt_en: A child who cannot see wants to find the tulsi plant in a garden full of plants. Using what you know about leaves, how could they find it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek bachcha jo dekh nahi sakta, bahut saare paudhon wale garden mein tulsi dhoondhna chahta hai. Patton ke baare mein jo pata hai uske hisaab se, woh tulsi kaise dhoondh sakta hai?
items.answer: By smell — gently rubbing leaves and sniffing for tulsi's strong smell; also by feeling the leaves' shape and texture.
hints: Which of our senses can tell leaves apart besides seeing?
What is special about tulsi leaves?
They could use their sense of ___.
By rubbing and smelling leaves — tulsi has a strong, special smell.

items.prompt_en: On the screen are three outline drawings: one with a single thick trunk, one with many thin stems from the ground, and one small with a soft stem. Label them herb, shrub and tree, and say one real plant for each.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe teen outline drawings hain: ek mein ek mota tana, ek mein zameen se kai patle tane, aur ek chhota naram tane wala. Inhe herb, shrub aur ped label karo, aur har ek ka ek asli paudha batao.
items.answer: Single thick trunk — tree (mango); many stems from the ground — shrub (rose or hibiscus); small with a soft stem — herb (wheat or coriander).
acceptable: trunk tree, many stems shrub, soft stem herb
hints: Which drawing is tallest with one trunk?
Which is bushy?
One trunk = ___; many stems = ___; soft stem = ___.
Tree (mango), shrub (hibiscus), herb (coriander).

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'Grass is not a plant because it is so small and has no flowers.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Ghaas paudha nahi hai kyunki woh bahut chhoti hai aur uspe phool nahi aate.'
items.answer: Wrong. Grass is a herb: it has roots, a stem and leaves, and it even makes tiny flowers.
hints: What parts does grass have if you pull one up?
Does being small stop something being a plant?
Grass has roots, a stem and ___, so it is a ___.
Wrong — grass is a small herb with roots, stem, leaves and tiny flowers.

items.prompt_en: Mithu wants to plant a garden. Teach Mithu the five groups — herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers — with one example each, and how to tell them apart.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu ek garden lagaana chahta hai. Mithu ko paanch group sikhao — herb, shrub, ped, climber aur creeper — har ek ka ek example, aur pehchaanne ka tareeka.
items.answer: Herb: small, soft green stem (coriander). Shrub: bushy with many woody stems (hibiscus). Tree: tall, one thick trunk (mango). Climber: weak stem that climbs a support (money plant). Creeper: weak stem that spreads on the ground (pumpkin).
acceptable: herb soft stem, shrub many woody stems, tree trunk, climber climbs, creeper spreads
hints: Start with how tall and how hard the stem is.
Then the two with weak stems.
Climbers go ___; creepers spread on the ___.
Herb-soft, shrub-bushy woody, tree-one trunk, climber-climbs support, creeper-spreads on ground.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what does a climber need to grow upwards?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ki baat: upar badhne ke liye climber ko kya chahiye?
items.answer: A support — a stick, wall, fence or another plant.
hints: Think of the money plant on the wall.
Its stem is weak.
It needs a ___ to hold on to.
A support, like a stick or a wall.

workedExample.problem: Sort a hibiscus bush, a coriander plant and a neem tree.
steps: Look at height and shape: coriander is small, hibiscus is bushy and medium, neem is tall.
Feel the stems gently: coriander's is soft and green; hibiscus has several hard, woody stems near the ground; neem has one thick woody trunk.
Match the clues: soft green stem = herb (coriander); many woody stems = shrub (hibiscus); one thick trunk = tree (neem).
Check: all three have roots, stems and leaves, so all three are plants.
fadedVersion: Look at height: coriander is small, hibiscus is ___, neem is tall.
Feel the stems: coriander soft; hibiscus has several ___ stems; neem one thick ___.
Soft green stem = ___; many woody stems = ___; one thick trunk = ___.
All three have roots, stems and leaves, so all are ___.

skills.title: Observe and name creatures that live on or visit a tree
Explain how parts of a plant give animals food (leaves, nectar, fruit, seeds) and shelter (branches, holes, leaves)
Predict what happens to animals when a tree is lost

expectations: One tree can be a home and food for many living things: birds, squirrels, ants, caterpillars, spiders, bees and lizards.
Different animals use different parts: nests in branches, holes in the trunk, and food from leaves, fruits, seeds or the nectar in flowers.
Insects, spiders and worms are animals too.
If a tree is cut down, many animals lose their homes and food — and even a fallen log becomes home and food for others.
We watch quietly from a distance and never disturb nests, eggs or hives.

misconceptions.belief: A tree is just a tree; nothing lives in it.
signs: Says 'only the tree is there'
Cannot name any creature that uses a tree
Guesses zero creatures for a tree watch

diagnostic.prompt_en: If you watch a big neem tree quietly for 10 minutes, what will you most likely see?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Agar tum ek bade neem ke ped ko 10 minute chupchaap dekho, toh sabse zyada kya dikhne ki ummeed hai?

options.text: Many living things — birds, ants, squirrels and insects
Nothing — trees are empty
Only the leaves moving in the wind

remediation.representation: Zoom-in photo series of one tree — canopy, bark, the underside of a leaf — revealing hidden creatures
remediation.moveShape: Predict a count, reveal the real count, then ask why the small ones were missed

misconceptions.belief: Insects, spiders and worms are not animals — 'animals' means big furry creatures.
signs: Says 'ants aren't animals, they're insects'
Lists only birds and monkeys when asked for animals in a tree

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these is an animal: a squirrel, an ant, a spider?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inme se jaanwar kaun hai: gilhari, cheenti, makdi?

options.text: All three
Only the squirrel
None of them

remediation.representation: Nested circles: 'animals' containing mammals, birds, insects, spiders and worms
remediation.moveShape: Ask what all animals do (eat, grow, move, breathe), then test the ant against that list

misconceptions.belief: A fallen, dead log is useless — nothing lives in it.
signs: Says 'it's dead, throw it away'
Expects an old log to stay unchanged forever

diagnostic.prompt_en: An old log has been lying on the forest floor for a year. Is anything using it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek purana lakdi ka lattha saal bhar se jungle mein zameen pe pada hai. Kya koi uska istemaal kar raha hai?

options.text: Yes — termites, beetles, ants and mushrooms live in it and slowly eat it
No — it's dead, so nothing lives there

remediation.representation: Time-lapse of a log over months: termites, mushrooms and beetles appear and it slowly crumbles into soil
remediation.moveShape: Contrast a fresh log with a year-old log; ask who moved in

items.prompt_en: Name three living things that might live on or visit a mango tree.
items.prompt_hi: Teen jeev batao jo aam ke ped pe reh sakte hain ya aate-jaate hain.
items.answer: Any three, e.g. birds (parrots, koels, crows), squirrels, ants, bees, caterpillars, spiders, bats, lizards.
hints: Who eats mangoes besides us?
Look closely at the bark and leaves too.
Birds like ___, a furry ___, and tiny ___.
For example: a parrot, a squirrel and ants.

items.prompt_en: How does a tree give food to animals? Tell me two different parts that animals eat.
items.prompt_hi: Ped jaanwaron ko khaana kaise deta hai? Do alag hisse batao jo jaanwar khaate hain.
items.answer: Any two, e.g. fruits (parrots, squirrels, bats), leaves (caterpillars, goats), nectar from flowers (bees, butterflies, sunbirds), seeds.
hints: What do caterpillars munch on?
What do bees drink from flowers?
Animals eat the tree's ___ and drink ___ from flowers.
For example: caterpillars eat leaves; bees drink nectar from flowers.

items.prompt_en: Before we start: if you sat still near one tree for 10 minutes, how many different kinds of creatures do you guess you'd spot? Say a number.
items.prompt_hi: Shuru karne se pehle: agar tum ek ped ke paas 10 minute chupchaap baitho, toh kitni alag-alag tarah ke jeev dikhenge? Ek number guess karo.
items.answer: Any guess is logged. The idea revealed after watching: there are usually more kinds than we expect, especially small ones like ants, spiders and insects.
hints: Think about birds first, then look smaller.
Have you counted the ants and spiders?
Most people guess too ___ because they miss the tiny ones.
Usually there are more kinds than we guess — the small creatures add up.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a big old peepal tree in the park is cut down. What will happen to the birds and squirrels that lived in it?
items.prompt_hi: Socho: park ka ek bada purana peepal ka ped kaat diya gaya. Usme rehne wale panchhiyon aur gilhariyon ka kya hoga?
items.answer: They lose their homes and food and must move away to find another tree; nests and eggs may be destroyed.
acceptable: they have to go somewhere else
hints: What did the tree give them?
Where will they sleep tonight?
They lose their ___ and their ___.
They lose their homes and food and have to search for a new tree.

items.prompt_en: Guess: a big branch falls off a tree in the forest and lies on the ground for a whole year. Will it be the same, or will things be living in and on it?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: jungle mein ek ped ki badi daali toot ke saal bhar zameen pe padi rahi. Kya woh waisi hi rahegi, ya usme aur uspe jeev rehne lagenge?
items.answer: Things will live in it — termites, beetles, ants and mushrooms; it slowly breaks down into soil.
hints: Is dead wood food for anyone?
Have you seen mushrooms on old wood?
Termites and ___ will move in, and it slowly becomes ___.
Creatures like termites, beetles and mushrooms move in and it slowly turns to soil.

items.prompt_en: Why do many birds build their nests high up in a tree's branches?
items.prompt_hi: Bahut saare panchhi apna ghosla ped ki oonchi daaliyon pe kyun banaate hain?
items.answer: It is safer there from cats, dogs and other animals that cannot reach, and the leaves hide the nest and give shade.
hints: Who might want to catch eggs or baby birds?
Can those animals climb thin high branches?
High up, the nest is ___ from cats and hidden by ___.
Safety — enemies can't reach easily, and leaves hide and shade the nest.

items.prompt_en: A squirrel and an ant both live on the same tree. Tell me one way they are different and one way they are the same.
items.prompt_hi: Gilhari aur cheenti dono ek hi ped pe rehti hain. Ek farak batao aur ek baat jo same hai.
items.answer: Different: size, number of legs (squirrel 4, ant 6), the squirrel has fur. Same: both are animals that get food and shelter from the tree.
acceptable: different size and legs; both are animals using the tree
hints: Count their legs.
Do both need food and a home?
Different: ___; same: both are ___ that use the tree.
Different size and legs; both are animals living off the tree.

items.prompt_en: Think of a hibiscus bush in a garden. Which creatures might use it, and for what?
items.prompt_hi: Garden ki ek gudhal ki jhaadi ke baare mein socho. Kaunse jeev iska istemaal karenge, aur kis liye?
items.answer: For example: bees, butterflies and sunbirds drink nectar from the flowers; ants climb on it; spiders make webs; caterpillars eat the leaves; small birds may shelter in it.
acceptable: bees drink nectar, spiders make webs
titli phool ka ras peeti hai
hints: Who visits the flowers?
Who might hide or hunt in the bush?
Bees visit for ___; spiders make ___.
Bees and butterflies for nectar, spiders for webs, caterpillars for leaves.

items.prompt_en: Your building wants to cut down a big tree in the compound to make parking space. Using what you know, what would you tell the people deciding?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari building parking ke liye compound ka ek bada ped kaatna chahti hai. Jo seekha hai uske hisaab se, faisla karne walon ko kya kahoge?
items.answer: The tree is home and food for many birds, insects and squirrels, and it gives shade; cutting it removes all of that, so keep it or find another space (and plant more trees).
acceptable: ped mein bahut jaanwar rehte hain
hints: Who lives in or visits that tree?
What else does the tree give the building?
The tree is a ___ for many animals and gives ___.
It's home and food for many creatures and gives shade — try to keep it.

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a drawing of a tree with empty spots: a hole in the trunk, a branch, a flower, and the ground by the roots. Drag a parrot, a bee, ants and a squirrel to where each might be, and tell me why.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe ek ped ki drawing hai, khaali jagahon ke saath: tane mein ek ched, ek daali, ek phool, aur jadon ke paas zameen. Tote, madhumakkhi, cheentiyon aur gilhari ko sahi jagah drag karo, aur batao kyun.
items.answer: Parrot in the hole (parrots nest in tree holes); squirrel on the branch; bee on the flower (nectar); ants on the ground near the roots or trunk.
acceptable: parrot hole, squirrel branch, bee flower, ants roots
hints: Where do parrots make nests?
What does a bee want from a tree?
The bee goes to the ___; the parrot to the ___.
Parrot–hole, squirrel–branch, bee–flower, ants–near the roots.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'Only big animals like monkeys and birds live in trees; ants and spiders don't count as animals.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Pedon mein sirf bade jaanwar jaise bandar aur panchhi rehte hain; cheenti aur makdi toh jaanwar hote hi nahi.'
items.answer: Wrong. Ants, spiders and caterpillars are animals too, and many of them live in trees.
acceptable: wrong, ants and spiders are animals
hints: Does an ant eat, move and grow?
What makes something an animal?
Ants and spiders ___, move and grow, so they are ___.
Wrong — ants and spiders are animals, and lots of them live in trees.

items.prompt_en: Mithu thinks a tree is just wood and leaves. Teach Mithu who lives in a tree and how the tree helps them.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu sochta hai ped bas lakdi aur patte hai. Mithu ko samjhao ped mein kaun rehta hai aur ped unki kaise madad karta hai.
items.answer: Many animals live in or visit a tree — birds, squirrels, ants, bees, caterpillars, spiders; the tree gives them homes (branches, holes) and food (leaves, fruits, nectar, seeds).
acceptable: many animals live there; the tree gives homes and food
hints: Name some animals first.
Then say what the tree gives each one.
The tree gives ___ and ___ to many animals.
Birds, squirrels and insects live there; the tree gives them shelter and food.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name two animals that get food from a tree, and say what they eat.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar wali baat: do jaanwar batao jinhe ped se khaana milta hai, aur woh kya khaate hain.
items.answer: Any two pairs, e.g. bees — nectar from flowers; parrots — fruits; caterpillars — leaves; squirrels — fruits and seeds.
hints: Think of flowers and fruits.
Who visits flowers? Who eats fruit?
Bees eat ___; parrots eat ___.
For example: bees drink nectar, parrots eat fruits.

workedExample.problem: Do a 10-minute tree watch on a neem tree with an adult.
steps: Sit quietly a few steps away from the tree so the animals are not scared; don't touch nests, hives or hairy caterpillars.
Look in layers: the top branches, the trunk and bark, the leaves (top and underside), and the ground near the roots.
For each creature, note what it is doing: eating, resting, building, hiding.
Sort what you saw: who used the tree for food, who used it as a home, and who used it for both.
fadedVersion: Sit ___ a few steps away so the animals are not scared.
Look in layers: top branches, ___, leaves, and the ground.
Note what each creature is ___.
Sort: food, home, or ___.

skills.title: Name small animals found in soil and leaf litter (earthworm, ant, beetle, millipede, woodlouse, termite)
Explain how soil animals help: earthworm tunnels let in air and water, and soil animals turn dead leaves into rich soil
Observe soil life safely: with an adult, use a stick, look without touching, put things back, wash hands

expectations: Soil is full of life: earthworms, ants, beetles, millipedes, termites and many tiny creatures live in it.
Earthworms are helpful: their tunnels let air and water into the soil, and they turn dead leaves into rich soil that helps plants grow.
Dead leaves and plants break down into soil with the help of soil animals and tiny living things too small to see.
We watch soil animals gently: with an adult, use a stick (not bare hands), look without grabbing, put stones and leaves back, and wash hands afterwards.

misconceptions.belief: Earthworms are harmful pests that spoil soil or eat crops.
signs: Says 'kill the worm, it spoils the soil'
Shows disgust and wants them removed from pots

diagnostic.prompt_en: A farmer finds lots of earthworms in her field. Is that good news or bad news?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek kisaan ko apne khet mein bahut saare kenchue milte hain. Yeh achhi khabar hai ya buri?

options.text: Good — earthworms make the soil loose and rich
Bad — earthworms eat the crops' roots

remediation.representation: Two-pot animation: soil with worm tunnels versus packed soil, with water poured on both
remediation.moveShape: Predict-observe-explain, then ask 'who made this soil better?'

misconceptions.belief: Soil is just dead dirt; nothing lives in it.
signs: Says 'soil is just mud'
Is surprised to find creatures under a stone or leaves

diagnostic.prompt_en: If you look closely at a handful of soil and leaves from under a tree, what might you find?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ped ke neeche se mutthi bhar mitti aur patte dhyaan se dekho toh kya mil sakta hai?

options.text: Tiny animals like ants, worms and beetles, and bits of dead leaves
Nothing alive — soil is just dirt

remediation.representation: Magnifier view of leaf litter with each creature circled as the child finds it
remediation.moveShape: Predict a count, then reveal

misconceptions.belief: Earthworms (and all small crawling things) are insects.
signs: Calls an earthworm or a spider an insect
Says all creepy-crawlies are insects

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is an earthworm an insect?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya kenchua ek keet (insect) hai?

options.text: No — insects have six legs; an earthworm has no legs and a long ringed body
Yes — all small crawling things are insects

remediation.representation: Leg-count cards: ant 6, spider 8, millipede many, earthworm 0
remediation.moveShape: Contrasting cases using the leg count as the deciding clue

items.prompt_en: Name two animals that live in the soil.
items.prompt_hi: Do jaanwar batao jo mitti mein rehte hain.
items.answer: Any two, e.g. earthworms, ants, beetles, termites, millipedes.
hints: Think of what comes out after rain.
Who builds hills of soil?
One is the long, wriggly ___, another is the ___.
For example, earthworms and ants.

items.prompt_en: How do earthworms help the soil? Tell me one way.
items.prompt_hi: Kenchue mitti ki madad kaise karte hain? Ek tareeka batao.
items.answer: Their tunnels let air and water into the soil; they make the soil loose; they turn dead leaves into rich soil.
acceptable: tunnels let air and water in
hints: What do earthworms leave behind as they move?
What do they eat?
Their ___ let air and water in.
They dig tunnels for air and water and turn dead leaves into rich soil.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: we pour the same cup of water on two pots — one with soil full of earthworm tunnels, one with hard, pressed-down soil. Which soaks it up faster?

items.answer: The soil with tunnels — water flows down through the holes; on packed soil the water sits on top or runs off.
hints: Where can water go in soil full of holes?
What happens to water on hard ground?
The soil with ___ soaks it up faster.
The tunnelled soil — water slips down the worm holes.

items.prompt_en: Predict: we put a layer of dead leaves on top of soil with earthworms in a pot and keep it damp for a few weeks. What will happen to the leaves?
items.prompt_hi: Socho: gamle mein kenchuon wali mitti ke upar sookhe patton ki parat bichha dein aur kuch hafte geela rakhein. Patton ka kya hoga?
items.answer: They will slowly disappear — earthworms pull them in and eat them, turning them into dark, rich soil.
acceptable: the leaves disappear into the soil
hints: What do earthworms eat?
What do they leave behind?
The leaves get eaten and turn into rich ___.
They slowly vanish — the worms turn them into dark, rich soil.

items.prompt_en: Before you look: when an adult lifts a flat stone in a damp garden after rain, using a stick, will the ground under it be empty, or will there be creatures? What kinds?
items.prompt_hi: Dekhne se pehle batao: baarish ke baad geele garden mein jab koi bada ek danda lagaake chapta patthar uthata hai, toh neeche zameen khaali hogi ya jeev honge? Kaun se?
items.answer: There will be creatures — earthworms, ants, beetles, woodlice (pill bugs) and millipedes like dark, damp places.
hints: Is it dark and damp under the stone?
Which creatures like that?
You'll find ___, ants and beetles.
Creatures — earthworms, ants, beetles and pill bugs hide there.

items.prompt_en: Why do so many soil animals live under stones and dead leaves rather than on open, dry ground?
items.prompt_hi: Itne saare mitti ke jeev khule sookhe maidan ki jagah pattharon aur sookhe patton ke neeche kyun rehte hain?
items.answer: It is dark, damp and cool there, and there is food (dead leaves); in the open they could dry out or be eaten.
acceptable: it's damp and dark and there's food
they would dry out in the sun
hints: What would the hot sun do to a soft earthworm?
What do they eat that's found under leaves?
It is ___ and dark there, with ___ to eat.
It's damp, dark and full of food, and they're safe from drying out.

items.prompt_en: An ant and an earthworm both live in soil. Which one is an insect, and how can you tell?
items.prompt_hi: Cheenti aur kenchua dono mitti mein rehte hain. Inme insect kaun hai, aur kaise pata chalega?
items.answer: The ant — it has six legs and three body parts; the earthworm has no legs and a long ringed body, so it is not an insect.
acceptable: the ant, because it has six legs
hints: Count the legs on each.
How many legs do insects have?
Insects have ___ legs, so the ___ is the insect.
The ant — six legs; the earthworm has none, so it isn't an insect.

items.prompt_en: A gardener adds vegetable peels and dry leaves to a compost pit. Which soil animals will help, and how?
items.prompt_hi: Ek maali compost ke gaddhe mein sabzi ke chhilke aur sookhe patte daalta hai. Kaunse mitti ke jeev madad karenge, aur kaise?
items.answer: Earthworms, ants, beetles and millipedes (and tiny living things too small to see) eat and break them down into compost, rich soil for plants.
acceptable: earthworms eat them and make compost
kenchue unhe khaad bana dete hain
hints: Which animal turned the leaves in the pot into soil?
What is compost?
___ and other soil animals break them into ___.
Earthworms and other soil animals break them down into compost.

items.prompt_en: A farmer sprays a strong poison on a field, and it kills all the earthworms too. What might happen to the soil after some years?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kisaan khet mein tez zeher chhidakta hai, jisse saare kenchue bhi mar jaate hain. Kuch saalon baad mitti ka kya ho sakta hai?
items.answer: The soil could become hard and less rich; air and water would not get in as well, so plants would grow less well.
acceptable: the soil becomes hard and poor
hints: What were the earthworms doing for the soil?
Who would dig the tunnels now?
Without worms the soil gets ___ and less ___.
It would get harder and poorer, and crops would suffer.

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a cut-away picture of soil with tunnels and a few dead leaves on top. Point to where an earthworm has been, and tell me in words what the tunnels do.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe mitti ka ek kata hua chitra hai — andar surangein aur upar kuch sookhe patte. Batao kenchua kahaan se guzra, aur shabdon mein samjhao surangein kya karti hain.
items.answer: The tunnels are the earthworm's paths; they let air and water go down to the roots.
acceptable: tunnels are worm paths that let air and water in
surangon se hawa aur paani andar jaata hai
hints: Find the winding lines in the soil.
What can travel down those lines?
The tunnels let ___ and ___ reach the roots.
Those are worm tunnels — they carry air and water down to the roots.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'To see soil animals, just push your hand under any stone and grab whatever is there.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Mitti ke jeev dekhne ho toh kisi bhi patthar ke neeche haath daalo aur jo mile pakad lo.'
items.answer: Wrong. Some creatures, like centipedes or scorpions, can bite or sting; an adult should lift the stone with a stick, you look without grabbing, put the stone back, and wash your hands.
acceptable: wrong, use a stick with an adult and don't grab
galat, bade ke saath danda lagao, pakdo mat
hints: Could anything under a stone bite or sting?
What should we use instead of our hands?
Use a ___ with an adult, look but don't ___.
Wrong — an adult lifts it with a stick, you only look, then put it back and wash hands.

items.prompt_en: Mithu thinks earthworms are yucky and bad. Teach Mithu what earthworms do for soil and plants.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu ko lagta hai kenchue gande aur bure hain. Mithu ko samjhao kenchue mitti aur paudhon ke liye kya karte hain.
items.answer: Earthworms dig tunnels that let air and water into the soil and make it loose; they eat dead leaves and turn them into rich soil, which helps plants grow — so they are helpers, not pests.
acceptable: they make tunnels and turn leaves into rich soil; they help plants
hints: What do the tunnels do?
What happens to the leaves they eat?
Tunnels let in ___ and ___; leaves become rich ___.
They aerate and loosen soil and turn dead leaves into rich soil — friends of plants.

items.prompt_en: From last time: is an earthworm an insect? Why or why not?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ki baat: kya kenchua insect hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
items.answer: No — it has no legs; insects have six legs.
hints: How many legs do insects have?
How many does an earthworm have?
Insects have six legs; an earthworm has ___.
No — an earthworm has no legs, so it isn't an insect.

workedExample.problem: Find out what lives in the leaf litter under a tree.
steps: With an adult, choose a damp spot under a tree with fallen leaves.

Put the leaves back so the creatures keep their home, and wash your hands with soap.
fadedVersion: With an ___, choose a damp spot under a tree.
Move the leaves with a ___ — no bare hands.
Look closely and ___ the kinds of creatures.
Put the leaves ___ and wash your hands.

skills.title: Give examples of animals depending on plants (food, shelter) and plants depending on animals (pollination, spreading seeds, enriching soil)

Can name honey as the only thing bees do

diagnostic.prompt_en: What would happen to the pumpkin flowers in a field if no bees visited them?

Nothing — flowers make fruits all by themselves
There would be more pumpkins, because bees eat them

misconceptions.belief: Plants don't need animals at all; only animals need plants.
signs: Says 'plants just need water and sun'
Can't explain how a seedling appears where nobody planted it

diagnostic.prompt_en: A peepal seedling is growing on top of a wall where nobody planted it. How did the seed get there?

options.text: A bird ate a peepal fruit and dropped the seed there
Plants don't need animals — it just appeared

remediation.representation: Story strip: a bird eats peepal figs → flies → drops a seed on a wall → a seedling sprouts

items.prompt_en: Name one way animals depend on plants.
items.prompt_hi: Ek tareeka batao jisme jaanwar paudhon pe nirbhar hain.
items.answer: For food (leaves, fruits, nectar, seeds) or for shelter (nests in trees, hiding in bushes).
hints: What does a cow eat?
Where does a sparrow build its nest?
Animals get ___ and ___ from plants.
Food and shelter — like grass for cows and trees for nests.

items.prompt_en: Name one way plants depend on animals.
items.prompt_hi: Ek tareeka batao jisme paudhe jaanwaron pe nirbhar hain.
items.answer: Bees and butterflies carry pollen so flowers can make fruits; birds spread seeds; dung and earthworms make the soil richer.
acceptable: madhumakkhi phoolon ki madad karti hai
hints: Who visits flowers all day?
How might a seed travel far away?
Bees carry ___; birds spread ___.
Bees carry pollen between flowers, and birds spread seeds.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: in a field of pumpkin plants, what would happen to the number of pumpkins if no bees or other insects visited the flowers?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: kaddu ke khet mein agar phoolon pe koi madhumakkhi ya keede na aayein, toh kaddu ki ginti ka kya hoga?
items.answer: Very few pumpkins would form — insects carry pollen between flowers, which the plant needs to make fruits.
hints: What do bees carry from flower to flower?
What does the flower need to become a fruit?
Without bees there would be very ___ pumpkins.
Very few — pumpkin flowers need insects to carry pollen.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if all the frogs in a rice field disappeared, what would happen to the insects there, and then to the rice?
items.prompt_hi: Socho: agar dhaan ke khet se saare mendhak gaayab ho jaayein, toh wahan ke keedon ka kya hoga, aur phir dhaan ka?
items.answer: The insects would increase because fewer frogs eat them, and they might eat more of the rice plants.
acceptable: keede badh jayenge aur fasal kharaab
hints: What do frogs eat?
If nobody eats the insects, how many will there be?
Insects would ___, and the rice would ___.
Insects would multiply and damage more rice.

items.prompt_en: You said birds help plants. Why does a bird eating a fruit help the plant?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha panchhi paudhon ki madad karte hain. Panchhi ka phal khaana paudhe ki madad kaise karta hai?
items.answer: The bird flies away and drops the seeds in a new place in its droppings, so new plants can grow far from the parent plant.
hints: What's inside the fruit?
Where does the bird go after eating?
The bird carries the ___ to a new ___.
It spreads the seeds to new places, where new plants can grow.

items.prompt_en: A cow gives us milk; a dung beetle gives us nothing we can use directly. Are both important? Tell me what each does.
items.prompt_hi: Gaay humein doodh deti hai; gobar ka keeda (dung beetle) humein seedhe kuch nahi deta. Kya dono zaroori hain? Batao har ek kya karta hai.
items.answer: Both are important: the cow gives milk and dung; the dung beetle breaks down and buries dung, cleaning up and returning it to the soil to make it richer.
acceptable: both are important; the beetle cleans up dung and feeds the soil
hints: What happens to dung on a field over time?
Who helps it disappear into the soil?
The beetle cleans up ___ and makes the soil ___.
Both matter — the cow gives milk, the beetle recycles dung into the soil.

items.prompt_en: Look at what you are wearing and your school things. Name two things that came from plants.
items.prompt_hi: Apne kapdon aur school ke saamaan ko dekho. Do cheezein batao jo paudhon se aayi hain.
items.answer: Any two, e.g. cotton clothes (cotton plant), paper and notebooks (wood from trees), a wooden pencil, a jute bag.
hints: What is your shirt made of?
What is paper made from?
Cotton comes from a ___; paper from ___.
For example, cotton clothes from the cotton plant and paper from trees.

items.prompt_en: In some places people spray so many insect-killing sprays that the bees disappear. Why might fruit farmers there have a big problem?
items.prompt_hi: Kuch jagahon pe log itni keede maarne wali dawaai chhidakte hain ki madhumakkhiyaan gaayab ho jaati hain. Wahan ke phal ugaane wale kisaanon ko badi pareshaani kyun hogi?
items.answer: Without bees, fewer flowers get pollinated, so fewer fruits form.
hints: What were the bees doing for the fruit trees?
Remember the pumpkin field.
Without bees, fewer flowers become ___.
Fewer fruits — the flowers lose their pollen carriers.

items.prompt_en: On the screen are cards: sun, grass, cow, people, dung, soil. Drag arrows to show who helps whom, then say your chain in one sentence.

items.answer: A correct loop such as: the sun helps grass grow; the cow eats grass; the cow gives milk to people and dung to the soil; rich soil helps grass grow better.
acceptable: sun to grass to cow to people, dung to soil to grass
hints: Start with what grass needs.
Where does the cow's dung end up?
Sun → ___ → cow → people, and dung → ___.
Sun grows grass, cow eats grass, gives milk and dung, dung feeds the soil, soil grows grass.

items.answer: Wrong. While drinking nectar, bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which many plants need to make fruits and seeds — the nectar is like a reward.
acceptable: galat, madhumakkhi parag le jaati hai
hints: What sticks to a bee's body?
Remember what happened to the no-bee pumpkin field.
Bees carry ___ that many plants need to make ___.
Wrong — bees carry pollen that many flowers need to become fruits.

items.prompt_en: Mithu thinks only animals that give us milk or eggs matter. Teach Mithu how plants, animals and people depend on each other, with two examples.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu sochta hai sirf woh jaanwar zaroori hain jo doodh ya ande dete hain. Mithu ko samjhao paudhe, jaanwar aur log ek doosre pe kaise nirbhar hain — do examples ke saath.
items.answer: Bees carry pollen so plants make fruits; birds spread seeds; frogs eat insects that harm crops; plants give food and shelter; people need plants and animals for food and clothes — every living thing has a place, even if it gives us nothing directly.
acceptable: bees and flowers, frogs and insects; every living thing matters
hints: Pick a pair that helps each other.
Pick an animal that gives us nothing but still matters.
Bees help ___; frogs help by eating ___.
Bees pollinate, frogs eat pests — all living things depend on each other.

items.prompt_en: From last time: how does a bee help a flower?

items.answer: It carries pollen from one flower to another, helping the plant make fruits and seeds.
hints: What sticks to the bee's body?
Where does it take it?
It carries ___ to the next flower.
It carries pollen between flowers so they can make fruits and seeds.

items.answer: Sunlight and the right amount of water (also soil, air and space).

Sunlight and just enough water.

items.prompt_en: In summer, what is one easy, safe way to help birds near your home?
items.prompt_hi: Garmi mein ghar ke paas ke panchhiyon ki madad ka ek aasaan aur safe tareeka batao.

A shallow bowl of clean water in the shade, refilled daily.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: two tulsi pots — one is watered only when its top soil feels dry; the other is flooded with water every few hours. After two weeks, which plant will be healthier?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: do tulsi ke gamle — ek mein paani sirf tab daalte hain jab upar ki mitti sookhi lage; doosre mein har kuch ghante mein bhar-bhar ke paani. Do hafte baad kaunsa paudha zyada swasth hoga?

Dirty water and mosquito wrigglers — change it daily.

items.prompt_en: Why can feeding monkeys at a tourist spot actually harm them?

arjun ka, chocolate kutte ke liye zeher hai

Regular morning/evening watering, a layer of dry leaves, and protection.

expectations: Plants give fruits and vegetables in particular seasons, so foods like mangoes (summer) and sarson ka saag (winter) are seasonal.

expectations: Pots and bricks are made from clay — a fine, sticky kind of soil — mixed with water and kneaded until smooth.

One triangle, two circles — next comes triangle, circle, circle.

Because the weaver puts in great skill and many hours of handwork.

Warli.

skills.title: Sort household waste into wet (kitchen and garden waste that rots) and dry (plastic, paper, metal, glass, cloth)
Know that some waste needs special care (broken glass, old batteries, old medicines — give them to an adult)
Explain where waste goes after the dustbin, and what happens to wet waste (it rots and can become compost) and dry waste (it can be reused or recycled)

expectations: Wet waste is food and plant waste that rots — peels, leftover food, tea leaves, flowers, garden leaves; it goes in the green bin and can become compost.
Dry waste is plastic, paper, metal, glass and cloth; it goes in the blue bin, and much of it can be reused or recycled.
We sort by what the waste is made of, not by whether it is wet: a wet plastic packet is still dry waste.
Waste doesn't disappear in the dustbin; trucks take it to sorting centres, compost pits or landfills, where it piles up.
Broken glass, old batteries and old medicines need special care — give them to an adult.

misconceptions.belief: Throwing waste in the dustbin makes it disappear.

Has no idea where the garbage truck goes

diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kachra gaadi kachra le jaati hai, uske baad woh kahaan jaata hai?

options.text: To a sorting place, a compost pit or a big landfill where it piles up
It disappears — it's gone forever

The wet (green) bin — because it's wet

remediation.representation: Sort-by-'made of' flowchart: is it from food or plants, so it will rot? → green; otherwise → blue
remediation.moveShape: Contrasting cases: a wet plastic packet next to dry fallen leaves

misconceptions.belief: Sorting doesn't matter — it all ends up in the same place anyway.
signs: Says 'why sort, it all goes in one truck'
Mixes peels and newspapers in one bag

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why do we keep wet and dry waste separate at home?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ghar pe geela aur sookha kachra alag kyun rakhte hain?

options.text: So wet waste can become compost and dry waste can be reused or recycled — mixed waste gets dirty and hard to use
It doesn't matter; it all ends up the same

remediation.representation: Animation of a mixed bin: peels make newspaper soggy and smelly, so neither can be used
remediation.moveShape: Ask what happens to a newspaper mixed with leftover dal overnight

items.prompt_en: Sort into wet or dry waste: banana peel, newspaper, plastic wrapper, leftover rice, glass bottle, tea leaves.
items.prompt_hi: Geele ya sookhe kachre mein baanto: kele ka chhilka, akhbaar, plastic ka rapper, bacha hua chawal, kaanch ki bottle, chai ki patti.
items.answer: Wet: banana peel, leftover rice, tea leaves. Dry: newspaper, plastic wrapper, glass bottle.
acceptable: wet peel rice tea leaves; dry newspaper wrapper bottle
hints: Which of these came from food or plants?
Which would rot in a few days?
Wet: peel, rice, ___; dry: newspaper, ___, bottle.
Wet: peel, rice, tea leaves. Dry: newspaper, wrapper, bottle.

items.prompt_en: What colour bin is usually used for wet waste in India, and what colour for dry waste?
items.prompt_hi: India mein geele kachre ke liye aam taur pe kaunse rang ka dabba hota hai, aur sookhe ke liye kaunse rang ka?
items.answer: Green for wet waste, blue for dry waste.
hints: Think of the colour of leaves for food and plant waste.
The other one is the colour of the sky.
Wet goes in ___; dry goes in ___.
Green for wet, blue for dry.

items.prompt_en: Try this with an adult: put some vegetable peels in a pot, cover them with soil and keep them damp. Before you check after 3–4 weeks — what will the peels look like? (Wash your hands afterwards.)
items.prompt_hi: Kisi bade ke saath try karo: kuch sabzi ke chhilke gamle mein daalo, upar se mitti dhak do aur geela rakho. 3–4 hafte baad dekhne se pehle batao — chhilke kaise dikhenge? (Baad mein haath dhona.)
items.answer: They will have mostly rotted and turned dark and soil-like — that is compost.
hints: What happens to old peels in the bin after a few days?
Remember the leaves in the earthworm pot.
They rot and become ___.
Mostly rotted into dark, soil-like compost.

items.prompt_en: Guess first: if peels and leftover dal are thrown in the same bag as newspapers, what will the newspapers be like a day later?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: agar chhilke aur bachi hui daal akhbaaron ke saath ek hi thaile mein daal dein, toh ek din baad akhbaar kaise honge?
items.answer: Wet, dirty and smelly — they can no longer be recycled easily; that's why we keep wet and dry waste apart.
acceptable: soggy and dirty, can't be recycled
hints: What does dal do to paper?
Would a recycler want soggy, smelly paper?
The newspapers become ___ and can't be ___.
Soggy and dirty — no longer good for recycling.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if the garbage truck didn't come to your area for two weeks in summer, what would happen to the bins and the street?
items.prompt_hi: Socho: agar garmi mein do hafte tak kachra gaadi tumhare area mein na aaye, toh dabbon aur gali ka kya haal hoga?
items.answer: Bins would overflow, wet waste would rot and smell, and flies, stray animals and germs would come — waste doesn't disappear by itself.
hints: Does waste vanish if nobody takes it?
What does rotting food attract?

They'd overflow and stink, attracting flies — waste doesn't vanish.

items.prompt_en: You put the wet milk packet in the dry bin. Why, even though it's wet?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne geela doodh ka packet sookhe dabbe mein daala. Geela hone ke baawajood kyun?
items.answer: Because it's plastic, which doesn't rot; we choose the bin by what the waste is made of, not by whether it is wet.
hints: What is the packet made of?
Will it rot like a peel?
It's ___, and plastic doesn't ___.
It's plastic — we sort by material, not by wetness.

hints: Which one came from a plant?
Which one will never rot?

Leaves to green (they rot), plastic bag to blue (it's plastic).

hints: Is broken glass safe to pick up?
Who should handle it, and how would they warn the waste collector?

Leave it; an adult wraps it up and labels it as broken glass.

items.prompt_en: Some cities have huge 'garbage mountains' called landfills. Using what you learned, how could your family help make them smaller?

items.answer: Sort waste so wet waste becomes compost and dry waste is recycled, and make less waste (cloth bags, reusing things).

What can wet waste become instead?

Sort it — compost the wet, recycle the dry, and make less waste.

items.answer: Rule: food and plant waste that rots goes in green; plastic, paper, metal, glass and cloth go in blue.
acceptable: things that rot go green, the rest go blue
jo sadta hai hara, baaki neela
hints: Ask of each picture: will it rot?
Then check what it's made of.

Rotting food and plant waste in green; plastic, paper, metal, glass, cloth in blue.

items.answer: Put food and plant waste that rots in the green bin and plastic, paper, metal, glass and cloth in the blue bin; give broken glass and batteries to an adult. Waste doesn't vanish — sorted wet waste becomes compost and dry waste can be recycled, while mixed waste piles up in landfills.

items.answer: The green bin (wet waste).

skills.title: Explain reduce, reuse and recycle with examples
Know that plastic does not rot like peels and lasts a very long time, and that burning waste harms the air
Suggest ways to reduce waste at home and school, and choose the best option (reduce first)

expectations: Reduce means making less waste in the first place (a cloth bag, a steel bottle, saying no to extra packets) — it is the best step.
Reuse means using things again (old jars for storage, bottles as planters, the back of paper).
Recycle means old things are broken down and made into new things (paper, glass, metal, some plastics) — it needs sorting first.
Plastic doesn't rot like vegetable peels; it stays in soil and water for a very, very long time and can harm animals.
Burning waste doesn't make it vanish — it makes harmful smoke.

Throws wrappers into the garden or compost

items.prompt_en: On the screen is a ladder with three steps: Reduce at the top, Reuse in the middle, Recycle at the bottom. Drag these actions to the right step: saying no to a straw, giving old clothes to a cousin, sending old notebooks for recycling. Then say why Reduce is at the top.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe teen seedhiyon wali ladder hai: sabse upar Reduce, beech mein Reuse, neeche Recycle. In kaamon ko sahi seedhi pe drag karo: straw ko mana karna, purane kapde cousin ko dena, purani copiyaan recycle bhejna. Phir batao Reduce sabse upar kyun hai.
items.answer: No straw — reduce; old clothes to a cousin — reuse; notebooks — recycle. Reduce is at the top because no waste is made at all.
acceptable: straw reduce, clothes reuse, notebooks recycle; reduce makes no waste
hints: Which action means the thing is never made or used?
Which one passes something on as it is?
Straw = ___, clothes = ___, notebooks = ___.
Straw–reduce, clothes–reuse, notebooks–recycle; reduce is top because it creates no waste.

items.prompt_en: Catch my mistake: 'The easiest way to get rid of plastic waste is to burn it — then it's gone.'
items.prompt_hi: Meri galti pakdo: 'Plastic ka kachra hatane ka sabse aasaan tareeka hai use jala do — phir woh khatam.'
items.answer: Wrong. Burning makes poisonous smoke and ash; the waste doesn't vanish, it goes into the air we breathe. Reduce, reuse and recycle instead.
hints: Where does the plastic go when it burns?
What would that smoke do to our lungs?
Burning makes harmful ___; it doesn't ___.
Wrong — burning turns plastic into toxic smoke; reduce, reuse, recycle instead.

items.prompt_en: Mithu buys a new plastic bag every time it goes shopping. Teach Mithu the three Rs, with an example of each, and which one is best.
items.prompt_hi: Mithu har baar shopping pe nayi plastic ki thaili leta hai. Mithu ko teen R sikhao, har ek ka ek example, aur kaunsa sabse achha hai.
items.answer: Reduce — make less waste, e.g. carry a cloth bag (the best one); Reuse — use things again, e.g. a jar for storage; Recycle — turn old things into new, e.g. newspapers into new paper. Plastic doesn't rot, so reducing it matters most.
acceptable: reduce cloth bag, reuse jar, recycle paper; reduce is best
hints: What should Mithu carry instead of a plastic bag?
Which R is at the top of the ladder?
Reduce: ___; reuse: ___; recycle: ___.
Reduce with a cloth bag (best), reuse jars, recycle paper.

items.prompt_en: From last time: which of the three Rs is the best, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar ka sawaal: teen R mein sabse achha kaunsa hai, aur kyun?
items.answer: Reduce — it stops waste from being made at all.
acceptable: reduce, because no waste is made

workedExample.problem: Make less waste from one family's weekly shopping.
steps: Look at the waste: plastic carry bags, plastic vegetable bags, a juice carton.
Reduce: carry cloth bags and a container from home so no new bags are needed.
Reuse: keep sturdy bags and jars to use again for storing things.
Recycle: rinse and send leftover packets and cartons to the kabadiwala or a recycling centre, sorted as dry waste.
